newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria aiming to boost oil in 'Vision 2010' - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria aiming to boost oil in 'Vision 2010' - paper.

text.p: Nigeria's government may be aiming to raise oil output capacity and reserves to four million barrels per day (bpd) and 40 billion barrels respectively under its "Vision 2010" programme, the official Daily Times newspaper reported on Monday.
There was no immediate comment from the petroleum ministry on the report.

Nigeria's current output capacity is two million bpd with reserves of 20 billion barrels which under a previous plan were to be raised by the year 2000 to 2.5 million bpd and 25 billion barrels respectively.
Daily Times said official thinking was that a daily output of four million barrels would serve as a bedrock for Nigeria's economic advancement in the 21st century.
It said the target would entail substantial funding of the upstream sector of Nigeria's oil industry.
Crude oil export contribute to well over 90 percent of Nigeria's total foreign exchange income.
